Country.evidence_source: [/page/18/Text/2] Such an approach to preventing hanging is feasible in prisons in contrast to the community (Gunnell et al., 2005). However, not all cells in all prisons in the UK have been converted to safer cells and not all prisoners at risk are identified as such and therefore accommodated in these locations.

Type.evidence_source: [/page/17/Text/8] The data from this study support the idea that ease of access to means of suicide is a determinant of the choice of method.

Area.evidence_source: [/page/17/Text/8] The data from this study support the idea that ease of access to means of suicide is a determinant of the choice of method. The most common reason for the method used was that it was the only one available because a prisoner could not obtain tablets or needles, was in an anti-ligature 'safer' cell or had no access to razors. So there was evidence of a substitution effect, but prisoners also took into consideration how quick and painful the alternative method was likely to be, as well as its likely consequences.
